parts.title: Three towns on a strait
parts.intro: Four Sicilian comuni lie close together around Etna (Piedimonte Etneo, Giarre, Mascali and Riposto), and on the other side of the strait are the Calabrian towns of Briatico and Scilla. The last chapter asks what the surnames mean, and how much it tells you that two people share one.

parts.title: Four grandparents, four families
parts.intro: Every person has four grandparents, and they are the honest unit of a family history: four separate families, four separate depths of evidence. These four were born within eight years of each other in three towns that had no connection. The chapters take the quarters in turn: Piedimonte Etneo (the Mazza and the Nicotra), Briatico (the Prostamo and the families around them), and Scilla (the Arena, and the Polistena).

parts.title: The crossings, and Brisbane
parts.intro: The family emigrated twice, in two waves half a century apart, to opposite sides of the world: the first went to America, the second to Australia, and both left from the same three towns. Every arrival after the Second World War came through Genoa, and in Brisbane four families from three towns became one.

parts.title: How the lines join
parts.intro: Every surname in this archive is here because a person married a person, and the marriages say which families came with whom. The Piedimonte Etneo Mazza who were once joined to the family by nothing are joined to it, and any person's aunts, uncles and cousins can be drawn, each line coloured by what joins the two. The family file arrived in separate pieces, and a file that draws as one tree is not necessarily one family.

parts.title: How we know, and what is missing
parts.intro: What this archive rests on, and for every line of it whether the document itself has been read or only an index to it. The investigations come next: the Sicilian and Queensland registers, the audit of searches that proved to be open, and the test of the claim that runs to 1697. Last come what has been read, the questions that remain, where a document and the family tree disagree, and what is being done as opposed to what is known.
